title: Microbucket reclamation and kernel-adaptive prefetch pacing for paged-attention KV stability
creator: Priya Shah
description: Problem: Under high-concurrency production traffic we observe worsening KV cache fragmentation and intermittent decode stalls on long-context agents. Current slab/window allocators cause a small number of large fragments to persist while many micro-slots remain underutilized; combined with aggressive prefill we see kernel handoffs that spike tail latency.
solution_summary: Introduce a microbucket reclamation layer plus a kernel-adaptive prefetch pacing controller. Microbuckets are thin allocation bins for small KV segments that enable cheap compaction and opportunistic migration without touching large slab compaction paths. The prefetch pacing controller uses live kernel latency and occupancy signals to throttle speculative prefill per-tenant and per-model, aligning prefill batches to kernels with compatible stride/sequence length to reduce cross-kernel thrash.
tasks: Design microbucket data structure and metadata footprint (memory budget <3% runtime heap)
Implement microbucket allocator and fast-path reclaim (lock-free heuristics for hot paths)
Add lightweight compaction pass for microbuckets during low-util epochs
Implement kernel-adaptive prefetch pacing controller and admission policy
Integrate occupancy estimator and kernel latency feedback (tracing hooks)
Add unit + fuzz tests for fragment invariants and allocator safety
e2e load test against synthetic long-context workloads and compare tail latency
acceptance_criteria: No correctness regressions on existing attention microbenchmarks
Tail decode latency (p99.9) under representative load reduced by >=15% or no worse than baseline
Effective fragmentation metric (measured as bytes-in-fragments / total-kv-bytes) reduced by >=20% after compaction pass
Memory overhead of microbucket metadata <3% of runtime KV memory budget
Canary rollout shows stable kernel-selection heatmap (no >10% unexpected kernel churn)
Feature gated behind runtime flag and documented in Console release notes
notes: We intentionally avoid adding a heavyweight global compactor in this iteration; focus is on low-latency, incremental reclamation and on aligning prefetch to current kernel topology. If microbucket reclamation shows durable gains we will follow up with cross-shard migration and a background compaction daemon in a separate ticket.
monitoring_and_observability: Add prefetch admission metrics: prefetch_allowed, prefetch_throttled, prefetch_kernel_mismatch_rate
Trace span tags for kernel selection reason and prefill_source
Dashboard: runtime-1.28 -> PagedAttention / KV / Microbucket overview
rollout_plan: Feature flag default off in runtime-1.28-canary
Canary in internal staging with synthetic long-context generator
Customer canary with low-risk tenants (non-critical workloads) -> monitor 48h
Gradual ramp to 25% fleet -> validate perf and error budgets
If stable promote to GA and flip default on
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Microbucket metadata overhead could increase memory pressure. Mitigation: strict metadata budget and eviction prioritizer that falls back to legacy allocator under pressure.

Risk: Throttling prefetch reduces cache hit rate and increases token cost. Mitigation: admission policy is model-aware and will only throttle when kernel-latency signals indicate thrash; will measure token cost delta in canary.
Risk: Interaction with Dedicated multi-tenant quotas. Mitigation: expose tenant-weighted admission controls and test on dedicated pools.
Risk: Regression in short-sequence latency due to compaction GC. Mitigation: compaction runs during low-util epochs and has abort-on-latency-spike safeguards.
